llm_dashboard_description: Provides real-time insights into model performance, including end-to-end latency and time to first token.
llm_dashboard_requests_tooltip: Shows the 95th and 99th percentile request latency.
llm_dashboard_requests_waiting_tooltip: Running is baseline batch load. Persistent Waiting means undersized capacity (add replicas). Swapped > 0 means KV cache was preempted — worst UX, add replicas or tune max_num_seqs.
llm_dashboard_models_tooltip: A sudden drop usually means a model was deleted or its pods crashed.
llm_dashboard_throughputs_tooltip: Tokens processed per second, split into prompt (input) and generation (output). Prompt much higher than generation = input-heavy workload (e.g. RAG, long context). Generation higher = output-heavy (e.g. chat, long replies). Both flat while latency is high = the bottleneck isn't throughput.
llm_dashboard_time_to_first_token_toolti: How long a user waits before seeing the first response token. Sudden spikes usually mean prefill is overloaded — long prompts, full batch, or saturated KV cache. Check KV Cache and Active Requests alongside this chart. Avg is Σ TTFT / requests over 5m; it keeps drawing under sparse traffic where p95/p99 drop out. Read it against the tail: Avg flat while p99 spikes = a few slow requests, all three rising = capacity.
llm_dashboard_time_per_output_token_tool: Time the model takes to generate each output token. Rising values mean decoding is slowing down, usually from GPU saturation or KV cache pressure. Avg is Σ TPOT / requests over 5m and matches benchmark reports that quote a mean; Avg flat while p99 spikes = a few slow requests, all three rising = capacity.
llm_dashboard_kv_cache_tooltip: Per-pod KV cache usage — direct indicator of load balance health. Pods moving together means router is fine; one pod hot while others are cold means routing problem.
llm_dashboard_queue_depth_tooltip: Brief spikes are fine, but persistent non-zero values mean overload. Waiting counts requests not yet batched (add replicas). Swapped means KV cache was preempted (worst UX, add replicas or tune max_num_seqs).
llm_dashboard_success_rate_tooltip: Below 100% means failures are occurring; check Analytics for the underlying cause.
llm_dashboard_total_requests_tooltip: Shown when the failure metric is unavailable. Reflects workload volume, not health.
llm_dashboard_finish_reason_tooltip: stop is normal completion and should dominate. length means max_tokens was hit and the response was truncated. abort means the client cancelled, usually a timeout. Rising length or abort signals upstream issues — compare with TTFT and E2E Latency.
llm_dashboard_e2e_latency_tooltip: If TTFT is fine but this is high, decoding is the bottleneck. A large p99 vs p95 gap means long-tail requests, often from KV cache pressure on long generations.
llm_dashboard_vgpu_tooltip: If KV Cache is low but a node's GPU memory is high, another workload is competing for the GPU. If both move together, vLLM itself is the consumer.
llm_dashboard_time_to_first_token_descri: First-token latency: mean, p95 and p99
llm_dashboard_time_per_output_token_desc: Inter-token latency: mean, p95 and p99
llm_dashboard_e2e_latency_description: End-to-end request latency at p95 and p99
llm_dashboard_per_pod_kv_cache_descripti: Per-pod KV cache utilization over time
llm_dashboard_prompt_size_description: Request rate by prompt token length
llm_dashboard_generation_size_descriptio: Request rate by generation token length

cluster_dashboard_node_pressure_descript: Per-node usage, request and limit vs allocatable
cluster_dashboard_node_pressure_tooltip: Usage is real consumption; Request is reserved capacity and drives scheduling; Limit is the ceiling — above 100% the node is over-committed. The GPU columns set what HAMi booked against what DCGM measures on the card. Rows are sorted so the most saturated node is on top; click a GPU node to open its per-card detail.
node_cpu_pressure_tooltip: Each node's CPU usage, request and limit, all as a percentage of its allocatable cores. The bar is sized and coloured by request, which is what actually constrains scheduling; a limit over 100% is ordinary burst-ceiling overcommit. Usage counts only what containers consume, so it reads lower than the node's own system charts. A limit is summed over the containers that declared one, so ⚠ marks a node where the rest are uncapped and the real ceiling is higher than the number. Click a node to drill into its detail.
node_memory_pressure_tooltip: Each node's working-set memory, request and limit, all as a percentage of its allocatable memory. The bar is sized and coloured by request, which is what actually constrains scheduling; a limit over 100% is ordinary burst-ceiling overcommit. Usage counts only what containers hold, so the node's own kernel and system memory sit outside it. A limit is summed over the containers that declared one, so ⚠ marks a node where the rest are uncapped and the real ceiling is higher than the number. Click a node to drill into its detail.
node_pod_density_tooltip: Each bar is one node's running pod count as a percentage of its allocatable pods (default 110). A node can be pod-saturated without being CPU or memory bound. Click a node to drill into its detail.
node_gpu_utilization_tooltip: Each bar is one node's average compute utilization across its GPU cards (DCGM). Only GPU nodes appear; ranked busiest first so idle, expensive capacity stands out at the bottom. Click a node to drill into its per-card detail.
node_restart_count_tooltip: Total container restarts on each node over the last hour (kube-state-metrics joined to the node label). Only nodes with restarts are shown — an empty list means no recent restarts. Bars turn orange at 1–10 and red above 10 (sustained crash-looping). Click a node to drill into its detail.
namespace_cpu_usage_tooltip: Each namespace's CPU usage, request and limit in cores side by side, ranked by declared limit. Usage is what the pods actually consume (cAdvisor); request and limit are summed from non-terminated pods only. Reading them together is what separates a large team from an over-declaration — a namespace holding a 7-core limit against 0.00 cores of usage booked a ceiling nobody uses. A limit is summed over the containers that declared one, so ⚠ marks a namespace where the rest are uncapped and the number is smaller than the real ceiling. Click a namespace to scope the pod detail below.
namespace_memory_usage_tooltip: Each namespace's working-set memory, request and limit side by side, ranked by declared limit. Usage is what the pods actually hold (cAdvisor); request and limit are summed from non-terminated pods only. All three print in one unit chosen for the whole card, so the rows stay comparable. A limit is summed over the containers that declared one, so ⚠ marks a namespace where the rest are uncapped and the number is smaller than the real ceiling. Click a namespace to scope the pod detail below.
namespace_gpu_usage_tooltip: GPUs (nvidia.com/gpu limits) allocated to ready pods per namespace (kube-state-metrics). Only namespaces using GPUs are shown. Click a namespace to scope the pod detail below.
namespace_restart_count_tooltip: Total container restarts per namespace over the last hour (kube-state-metrics). Only namespaces with restarts are shown — an empty list means no recent restarts. Bars turn orange at 1–10 and red above 10 (sustained crash-looping). Click a namespace to scope the pod detail below.
pvc_storage_usage_tooltip: Used capacity per PersistentVolumeClaim. Near 100% risks running out of space.
node_detail_cpu_tooltip: Non-idle CPU across all cores right now. Sustained highs mean the node is compute-bound.
node_detail_ram_tooltip: Memory in use as % of installed RAM. Above 90% may trigger OOM kills.
node_detail_swap_tooltip: How much swap is occupied. Any sustained swap usage on a Kubernetes node usually signals memory pressure and hurts latency. 0% is healthy.
node_detail_filesystem_tooltip: Used capacity of the root filesystem. Above 85% risks disk-pressure evictions.
node_detail_uptime_tooltip: How long this node has been part of the cluster, measured from its creation timestamp.
node_chart_cpu_core_tooltip: CPU time split by mode across all cores. High iowait signals a storage bottleneck; the stacked total is overall utilisation.
node_chart_ram_tooltip: Memory split into used, buffers, cache and free. Growing used with shrinking free is normal until cache can no longer be reclaimed — that is when pressure starts.
node_chart_disk_rw_tooltip: Bytes/s read from and written to disk; sustained highs with high I/O time mean a disk bottleneck.
node_chart_disk_io_tooltip: Share of time the disk was busy. Near 100% means it is saturated and requests queue.
node_chart_network_rx_tooltip: Bytes per second received per network interface. Compare with transmitted to spot asymmetric flows; the filter limits to the busiest interfaces.
node_chart_network_tx_tooltip: Bytes per second transmitted per network interface. Sudden sustained spikes can indicate large data transfers or replication traffic.
node_chart_gpu_util_tooltip: Per-card GPU compute utilization. Sustained highs mean the GPUs are well used; lows on a busy node suggest the bottleneck is elsewhere (data loading, CPU, network).
node_chart_gpu_memory_tooltip: Per-card GPU memory in use as a percentage of each card's framebuffer. Near 100% risks out-of-memory workloads.
node_chart_gpu_power_tooltip: Per-card power draw in watts. Tracks how hard each GPU is working and helps spot power or thermal ceilings.
node_chart_gpu_temp_tooltip: Per-card GPU temperature in °C. Sustained high temperatures can trigger thermal throttling and lower performance.
node_detail_pods_tooltip: Scheduled pods vs the node capacity. Near 100% no more pods fit, even with free CPU/memory.
node_chart_cpu_commit_tooltip: CPU as % of allocatable cores. Request drives scheduling; a Limit over 100% means the node is over-committed.
node_chart_mem_commit_tooltip: Memory as % of allocatable. Request drives scheduling; a Limit over 100% risks OOM eviction under pressure.
node_chart_network_io_tooltip: Bytes/s received and transmitted across all interfaces (excludes loopback).
pod_detail_table_description: Per-pod requests, limits and live usage
pod_detail_table_tooltip: Requests and limits for each pod, the way kubectl describe node reports them; hover one to see its share of the owning node's allocatable capacity. Usage shows what the pod is actually consuming and is colored by how close it sits to its own limit. Click any header to sort. GPU columns read — for pods that hold no GPU: Cards is the nvidia.com/gpu count, while Allocated, Usage and Utilization come from HAMi, so a pod that bypassed the scheduler shows cards but no memory.
workload_kpi_pods_tooltip: Running pods in the current scope.
workload_kpi_cpu_tooltip: Live CPU cores used by containers in scope.
workload_kpi_memory_tooltip: Live working-set memory used by containers in scope.
workload_kpi_restarts_tooltip: Container restarts in the last hour; a rising count points to unhealthy workloads.
ns_commit_cpu_tooltip: Namespace CPU in cores: Usage vs Request vs Limit. Request far above Usage wastes scheduling quota.
ns_commit_mem_tooltip: Namespace memory: Usage vs Request vs Limit. Usage near Limit risks OOM kills.
llm_dashboard_top_throughput_tooltip: Models processing the most tokens per second right now (prompt + generation combined). Compare with KV Pressure to tell heavy load from actual saturation.
llm_dashboard_top_kv_pressure_tooltip: Highest KV cache usage among each model's pods. Above 85% means requests can be preempted (worst user experience). Low throughput with high pressure means a long-context workload, not high traffic.
llm_dashboard_top_p99_latency_tooltip: Slowest 1% of requests per model — the worst experience users actually see. Models appearing on all three top charts should be tuned first.
llm_dashboard_top_requests_tooltip: Requests each model is handling right now, shown as running / waiting (green = running on the GPU, orange = queued in the scheduler). A waiting count that keeps growing means the model is at capacity — check KV Pressure to tell memory-bound from compute-bound, then scale replicas or raise max_num_seqs.
llm_dashboard_active_requests_tooltip: Requests being processed (Running) vs. queued up (Waiting). Some Running is normal load. If Waiting stays above zero, capacity is undersized — add replicas. Brief spikes under heavy traffic are expected.
llm_dashboard_per_pod_kv_cache_tooltip: Each line is one pod's KV cache usage. Lines moving together = the router is balancing fairly (add replicas if they're all high). One pod high while others are low = traffic is being routed unevenly.
llm_dashboard_prefill_decode_tooltip: The two stages of inference: prefill processes the input prompt, decode generates the output. Prefill ≫ Decode = input is the bottleneck (raise tensor parallelism, enable prefix cache). Decode ≫ Prefill = output is the bottleneck (add replicas, tune max_num_seqs).
llm_dashboard_prefix_cache_tooltip: How often vLLM reuses cached prompt prefixes instead of recomputing them. High hit rate = TTFT stays low and throughput is good. Low hit rate = cache is too small, or prompts share little prefix (system prompt placed late, every user starts differently).
llm_dashboard_cache_tiers_tooltip: Hit rate at each cache layer a request falls through. vLLM is the prefix cache in GPU VRAM; the middleware is the KV store behind it, which manages DRAM and SSD behind a single lookup. The middleware only sees what vLLM missed, so vLLM has the biggest TTFT impact. vLLM high = most prompts reuse the GPU cache. vLLM low but middleware high = offload is catching the misses (VRAM alone is too small). No middleware line = offload isn't enabled for this scope. LMCache's own DRAM in front of the middleware is a staging buffer rather than a tier that serves hits, so it has no line of its own. Everything found below vLLM comes from the middleware, so both rates are read from vLLM's own counters in the same unit. Their denominators still differ — the middleware is only asked for what vLLM missed — so read each line's own trend rather than the gap between them.
llm_dashboard_prompt_size_tooltip: Distribution of incoming prompt lengths — tells you what kind of workload this is. Concentrated short = chat. Concentrated long = RAG or document QA (raise max_model_len, enable prefix cache). Two peaks (short and long mixed) = consider splitting short and long traffic into separate deployments.
llm_dashboard_generation_size_tooltip: Distribution of response lengths. Concentrated short = classification or extraction (decode is not the bottleneck). Concentrated long = agent or writing tasks (decode-bound risk — watch TPOT and replica count).
llm_dashboard_per_replica_throughput_too: Tells you whether adding replicas actually helped. Per-pod throughput stays steady after scaling = each pod still has work (traffic is also growing). Per-pod drops = traffic is being split (scaling worked). Big gaps between pods = a load-balancing problem.

cluster_dashboard_gpu_memory_tooltip: Allocated is GPU memory the HAMi scheduler handed out to pods; Used is what DCGM measures as actually resident on the cards; Utilization is the share of time a kernel was executing. A booking far above usage means capacity is reserved but idle. Usage above the booking means a workload escaped HAMi — a pod setting NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all, or requesting a bare nvidia.com/gpu.

no_gpu_for_model: No GPU detected for this model
llm_dashboard_pod_hardware_status_toolti: Pod & GPU health at a glance: Restart / OOM / XID / Preempt (24h), CPU Throttle (5m), and Shm (SIGBUS) crashes. Look into anything orange or red before tuning serving params.
llm_dashboard_cpu_throttle_hint: Share of CPU periods that were throttled (last 5 min). Sustained throttling slows tokenizer and request handling, indirectly raising TTFT — raise the CPU limit if this stays above 25%.
llm_dashboard_shm_crash_hint: Counts pods whose last crash was exit 135 (SIGBUS) — typically a full /dev/shm, which vLLM uses for engine↔worker IPC (the default is only 64 MB). Fix by enlarging it (emptyDir medium: Memory / --shm-size). Heuristic — SIGBUS has other causes too, and OOMKilled is a separate memory-limit issue.
llm_dashboard_preempt_hint: Requests evicted from the GPU over the last 24h because the KV cache ran out — they get re-prefilled, spiking TTFT and wasting compute. 0 = healthy. Sustained preemptions = lower max_num_seqs, add GPU memory, or enable KV cache offload.
llm_dashboard_prefix_caching_hint: Whether vLLM Automatic Prefix Caching (APC) is enabled for this model — the on-GPU L1 cache that reuses shared prompt prefixes. On = the L1 Cache Hit by Tier line is meaningful. Off = every request recomputes its prefix, so prefix cache hit rate stays at 0 by design.
llm_dashboard_memory_usage_no_limit_bann: No memory limit set — showing absolute GiB
llm_dashboard_memory_usage_tooltip: >90% = OOMKill risk; 70–90% = tight. When Pod Health shows OOM > 0, use this chart to find the affected pod.
llm_dashboard_gpu_memory_tooltip: >95% = node full (add GPUs or replicas); 80–95% = warm; <80% = vLLM over-reserved KV. Counts all workloads on the node, not just this model.

license_provisional_banner_desc: Currently using a provisional license with limited features. Please follow the steps below to apply for an official license.
license_provisional_step1: Click "Export License Request" in the top-right, generate and download the .lreq file
license_provisional_step2: Submit the .lreq to the vendor through official channels for signing
license_provisional_step3: After review, the vendor will provide an official .lic license file
license_provisional_step4: After receiving the .lic, click "Import License" in the top-right to complete the upgrade
license_upload_missing_fields: Please provide a license name and select a .lic file
license_import_parse_error: Unable to parse the license file. The token payload must contain exactly one software entry.
license_overwrite_confirm_description: License "{name}" is currently Active. Uploading will overwrite it (renewal) and take effect immediately. Click again to confirm.
license_adjust_nodes_override_rejected: Node override was rejected due to quota violation. Nodes have reverted to FIFO order.
license_adjust_nodes_fifo_hint: FIFO mode: nodes are authorized in the order they joined the cluster.
license_adjust_nodes_readonly: This license has expired or is invalid. Node adjustments are not allowed.
alerting_description: Email platform alerts through an SMTP server.
cluster_no_alerts_firing: No alerts are firing for the nodes, the control plane, storage or monitoring.
needs_attention_tooltip: Alerts about the cluster itself: nodes, the control plane, capacity, storage and monitoring. Critical first, then oldest first. Workload alerts, such as a failed job or a crashing pod, are left to each workspace.
cluster_dashboard_storage_tooltip: Used is raw Ceph capacity in use across every OSD, replicas included. aiDAPTIV is the share of the local aiDAPTIVCache drives (TopoLVM) in use, summed across nodes.
control_plane_tooltip: etcd and the Kubernetes API server run as static pods on every master. etcd keeps working while more than half of its members are up.
platform_services_tooltip: Each service runs as a single instance. If its node goes offline, Keycloak, Harbor and Prometheus need a manual step before they can start on another node.
gpu_no_data_not_responding: No GPU data while the node is not responding.
alert_kube_node_not_ready_desc: Its Ready condition is false. Pods on it move to other nodes after about 5 minutes.
alert_kube_node_unreachable_desc: Kubernetes marked it unreachable, so no new pods are scheduled there.
alert_kube_node_readiness_flapping_desc: It switched between Ready and NotReady several times in 15 minutes.
alert_kubelet_down_desc: Prometheus cannot scrape one or more kubelets, so pod metrics from those nodes are missing.
alert_kubelet_too_many_pods_title: Node {node} is near its pod limit
alert_kubelet_too_many_pods_desc: New pods may not fit on this node.
alert_node_filesystem_space_filling_up_d: At the current rate it runs out of space within a day.
alert_node_filesystem_almost_out_of_spac: Less than 5 % of its space is left.
alert_node_filesystem_files_filling_up_t: Disk {mountpoint} on {instance} is running out of inodes
alert_node_filesystem_files_filling_up_d: At the current rate it runs out of inodes within a day.
alert_node_memory_high_utilization_title: Memory on {instance} is almost used up
alert_node_memory_high_utilization_desc: More than 90 % of the node’s memory is in use.
alert_node_cpu_high_usage_desc: CPU use has stayed above 90 % for 15 minutes.
alert_node_clock_not_synchronising_desc: NTP is not keeping the clock in sync. Certificates and logs can be affected.
alert_kube_pod_not_ready_desc: It has not become ready in {namespace} for over 15 minutes.
alert_kube_container_waiting_desc: Pod {pod} in {namespace} has waited over an hour for it to start.
alert_kube_deployment_replicas_mismatch_: Fewer replicas are available in {namespace} than requested.
alert_kube_deployment_rollout_stuck_desc: The rollout in {namespace} is not progressing.
alert_kube_stateful_set_replicas_mismatc: Fewer replicas are ready in {namespace} than requested.
alert_kube_stateful_set_update_not_rolle: Update of {statefulset} has not rolled out
Not every replica in {namespace} runs the new revision.
alert_kube_daemon_set_rollout_stuck_desc: Not every node runs the updated pod from {namespace}.
alert_kube_daemon_set_not_scheduled_desc: Some nodes that should run it from {namespace} do not.
alert_kube_daemon_set_mis_scheduled_desc: Pods from {namespace} run on nodes they should not.
alert_kube_job_failed_desc: The job in {namespace} did not complete.
alert_kube_job_not_completed_desc: The job in {namespace} has run for over 12 hours.
alert_kube_hpa_maxed_out_desc: The autoscaler in {namespace} cannot add more replicas.
alert_kube_persistent_volume_filling_up_: The volume in {namespace} is running out of space.
alert_kube_persistent_volume_errors_desc: Its phase is Failed or Pending.
alert_kube_cpu_overcommit_title: CPU requests leave no room for a node failure
alert_kube_cpu_overcommit_desc: If a node goes down, its pods cannot all be rescheduled on the others.
alert_kube_memory_overcommit_title: Memory requests leave no room for a node failure
alert_kube_memory_overcommit_desc: If a node goes down, its pods cannot all be rescheduled on the others.
alert_cpu_throttling_high_desc: Pod {pod} in {namespace} is throttled more than a quarter of the time.
alert_kube_api_down_desc: Prometheus cannot reach any API server.
alert_kube_api_error_budget_burn_title: The Kubernetes API is returning errors
alert_kube_api_error_budget_burn_desc: Errors or slow responses are using up its error budget quickly.
alert_kube_client_certificate_expiration: A certificate used to reach the API server expires within a week.
alert_kube_version_mismatch_desc: Not every control-plane and node component runs the same version.
alert_etcd_members_down_desc: One or more etcd members cannot be reached.
alert_etcd_insufficient_members_desc: Too few etcd members are up to keep the cluster writable.
alert_etcd_no_leader_title: An etcd member has no leader
alert_target_down_desc: Prometheus cannot reach some {job} targets in {namespace}.
alert_prometheus_rule_failures_desc: Some alerting or recording rules fail, so their alerts may never fire.
alert_ceph_health_error_title: Ceph is in an error state
alert_ceph_health_error_desc: Ceph reports HEALTH_ERR. Some data may be unavailable.
alert_ceph_health_warning_desc: Ceph reports HEALTH_WARN. Data stays available.
alert_ceph_osd_down_desc: Ceph keeps fewer copies of some data until the OSD returns.
alert_ceph_mon_down_desc: Ceph still has quorum, but has less room for another failure.
alert_ceph_cluster_near_full_desc: Ceph has used over 85 % of its raw capacity.
alert_ceph_cluster_critically_full_desc: Ceph has used over 90 % of its raw capacity and will soon stop accepting writes.
alert_control_plane_not_scraped_desc: Their pods are healthy (kube-proxy, if listed, is not deployed), but Prometheus cannot scrape {components}, so problems there will not raise alerts.
entry_points_tooltip: Each reserved IP is answered by one master at a time. If that master fails, another master takes the IP over and the address stays the same.
platform_checks_tooltip: Read from the cluster every minute. Modules are the Flux HelmReleases OtterScale installs. Backup is Velero. Certificates are the ones cert-manager manages; a certificate you supplied yourself is not checked. Notifications says whether Alertmanager sends alerts anywhere.
analytics_ranking_now_hint: Now. Select a row to see its details.
analytics_ranking_history_hint: Average over {window}. Select a row to see its details.
analytics_occupancy_tooltip: Each block is one pod on this node, grouped by workspace. Its area is its share of the selected resource. Hover a block for all its numbers; every number is also in the table below.
analytics_gpu_summary_allocated: Allocated {allocated} of {total} GiB ({pct}%) · in use {used} GiB
analytics_gpu_summary_usage: In use {used} of {total} GiB ({pct}%) · {outside} GiB outside HAMi
analytics_limit_overcommit_note: Limits add up to more than the node can give, so the map shows each pod's share of the total limits and no unallocated space.
analytics_map_needs_width: The map needs a wider screen. Every value is in the table below.
analytics_not_tied: {x} GiB, not tied to any pod
analytics_pods_units: CPU in cores · memory in GiB
alert_hami_gpu_memory_used_beyond_alloca: GPU memory in use outside HAMi on {node} {device}
{used} GB in use, but HAMi allocated {alloc} GB. {diff} GB is used by something that skipped HAMi, so pods on this card can run out of memory.
alert_hami_gpu_memory_over_allocated_des: Allocations add up to {alloc} GB on a {cap} GB card. If every pod uses its full share, one of them will fail.
time_range_ends_midnight: Past day: the window ends at its midnight.
usage_note_tokens: Token counts include only requests that report usage. A streaming client reports it only when it sets stream_options.include_usage; its requests are counted either way.
usage_deleted_keys_note: Usage from keys that no longer exist
usage_users_matched: Users are matched through the creator recorded on each API key.
usage_empty_title_last: No API key requests in the last {span}
usage_empty_title_range: No API key requests in this time range
usage_empty_desc: Requests made with an API key through AI Gateway show up here within a minute. Requests sent to a model without an API key are only counted in Overview and Analytics.
usage_not_collected_title: AI Gateway usage isn't being collected
usage_not_collected_desc: Prometheus has no AI Gateway metrics. A platform administrator needs to enable scraping of the AI Gateway (the Agent Router ext_proc metrics); usage then shows up here within a minute.
usage_keys_unreadable: API keys couldn't be read, so usage can't be matched to the people who made the keys. API keys, Workspaces and models are still shown.
model_overview_models_note: Latency is p95 over the last 5 minutes. Select a model to open it in Analytics.
model_overview_metrics_failed: Couldn't load engine metrics. Numbers and status may be incomplete.
model_overview_list_failed: Couldn't list models. Replicas are unknown.
model_overview_kv_by_model_note_top: Busiest pod · top {shown} of {total} by requests
model_analytics_note_starting: This model is still starting. Its pods are not ready yet, so there are no engine metrics.
model_analytics_note_idle: This model is running but received no requests in this range.
model_analytics_cache_tiers: Prefix cache hit rate by tier
model_analytics_gen_per_replica: Generation tokens per second per replica
model_analytics_used_vs_hami: Used against the HAMi allocation ({quota} GiB)
model_analytics_empty_desc: Models deployed from AI Studio show up here once their engine starts reporting metrics.
storage_health_line_warn: Data is readable and writable. Nothing is lost.
storage_health_line_unavailable: Some data can't be read or written until its placement groups are active again.
storage_health_line_full: Writes are stopped because storage is full. Reads still work.
storage_health_line_unfound: Some objects can't be found. Data may be lost.
storage_health_line_err: Ceph reports an error. The checks say what is affected.
storage_health_checks_tooltip: Checks Ceph raises right now that affect data or service, with what they mean and what to do. Configuration reminders are counted under the list. How long a check has run is read from the last 7 days.
storage_check_unknown_desc: No description for this check yet; see the Ceph documentation for {code}.
storage_raw_tooltip: Bytes used on every OSD, copies included, as a share of all OSD space.
storage_data_stored_tooltip: Data in all pools before copies. The bar is its share of usable space: data stored plus what can still be written.
storage_promised_tooltip: Storage requested by PVCs on Ceph StorageClasses, as a share of usable space. Thin provisioning lets it pass 100 %.
storage_fullest_tooltip: The fullest OSD sets when writes stop: Ceph warns at the nearfull ratio and stops writes at the full ratio, both read from the cluster.
storage_pools_header_growing: Shared space fills in about {duration} at the 7-day pace; {pool} grows fastest.
storage_pools_header_over: Shared space lasts more than 5 years at the 7-day pace; {pool} grows fastest.
storage_pools_tooltip: Growth is the 7-day average. Pools on the same OSDs share one free space, so it fills before any single pool would.
storage_check_osd_nearfull_desc: Ceph stops writes to every pool on this OSD at {full}. Rebalance data or add capacity.
storage_check_osd_backfillfull_title: {osd} is too full to take backfill ({pct})
storage_check_osd_backfillfull_desc: Ceph will not move data onto it, so recovery can stall. Rebalance data or add capacity.
storage_check_osd_full_desc: Writes to every pool on this OSD are stopped. Delete data or add capacity now.
storage_check_pool_nearfull_title: A pool is nearly at its quota
storage_check_pool_nearfull_desc: Writes stop when the pool reaches its quota. Raise the quota or delete data.
storage_check_pool_full_desc: Writes to the pool are stopped. Raise its quota, delete data or add capacity.
storage_check_pg_degraded_title: Some data has fewer copies than it should
storage_check_pg_degraded_desc: Data is still readable and writable. Ceph restores the missing copies as OSDs return and recovery runs.
storage_check_pg_availability_title: Some data can't be read or written
storage_check_pg_availability_desc: Some placement groups are not active. Bring the missing OSDs back online.
storage_check_pg_damaged_desc: Some placement groups are inconsistent. Repair them.
storage_check_pg_recovery_full_title: Recovery is blocked by full OSDs
storage_check_pg_recovery_full_desc: Data can't be recovered onto OSDs past the full ratio. Add capacity or rebalance.
storage_check_pg_backfill_full_title: Backfill is blocked by full OSDs
storage_check_pg_backfill_full_desc: Data can't be moved onto OSDs past the backfillfull ratio. Add capacity or rebalance.
storage_check_object_unfound_desc: Ceph knows these objects exist but has no copy of them. Bring offline OSDs back before marking anything lost.
storage_check_osd_scrub_errors_desc: Some object copies don't match. Repair the affected placement groups.
storage_check_pool_no_redundancy_title: Some pools keep only one copy
storage_check_pool_no_redundancy_desc: If the disk holding it fails, that data is lost. Raise the pools' size once there are enough OSDs.
storage_check_too_few_osds_title: Fewer OSDs than the pools need
storage_check_too_few_osds_desc: Ceph can't put each copy on its own OSD. Add OSDs.
storage_check_osd_down_title: One or more OSDs are down
storage_check_osd_down_desc: Their data is served from other copies, if there are any. Check the OSD pods and disks.
storage_check_osd_host_down_desc: Every OSD on it is unavailable. Check the host.
storage_check_mon_down_title: A monitor is out of quorum
storage_check_mon_down_desc: The cluster keeps working while a majority of monitors remains. Check the monitor pod.
storage_check_mon_disk_low_title: A monitor is low on disk space
storage_check_mon_disk_low_desc: Free space on its host before it reaches the critical level and the monitor shuts down.
storage_check_mon_disk_crit_title: A monitor is critically low on disk space
storage_check_mon_disk_crit_desc: The monitor shuts down when its disk fills. Free space on its host now.
storage_check_mon_clock_skew_desc: Clock drift can break quorum. Check time sync on the monitor hosts.
storage_check_mgr_down_desc: Metrics and this dashboard stop updating. Check the manager pods.
storage_check_mds_insufficient_standby_d: If the active metadata server fails, CephFS pauses until it restarts. Add a standby.
storage_check_fs_degraded_desc: Some metadata server ranks are not active, so file access may stall. Check the metadata servers.
storage_check_mds_slow_metadata_io_title: A metadata server is waiting on slow storage
storage_check_mds_slow_metadata_io_desc: File operations are slow because its metadata pool answers slowly.
storage_check_fs_with_failed_mds_title: A CephFS filesystem has a failed metadata server
storage_check_fs_with_failed_mds_desc: File access stops until another metadata server takes over. Check the metadata servers.
storage_check_slow_ops_desc: Requests have waited longer than 30 seconds. Check for busy or failing disks.
storage_check_recent_crash_desc: It restarted, and the crash is kept for review. Archive it once checked.
storage_check_auth_insecure_keys_allowed: The cluster still accepts keys of an older, weaker type. Rotate the keys, then turn the old type off.
storage_check_auth_insecure_client_key_t: Some clients use an insecure key type
Rotate those clients' keys to the current type.
storage_check_auth_insecure_keys_creatab: Insecure keys can still be created
New keys may be made with the older, weaker type. Turn that option off.
storage_check_pool_app_not_enabled_title: A pool has no application set
storage_check_pool_app_not_enabled_desc: Tag the pool as rbd, cephfs or rgw so Ceph knows what uses it.
storage_check_osdmap_flags_desc: Flags such as noout or norebalance change how Ceph handles failures. Clear them after maintenance.
storage_check_too_many_pgs_title: Too many placement groups per OSD
storage_check_too_many_pgs_desc: Each OSD carries more placement groups than recommended, which costs memory. Add OSDs or reduce placement groups.
storage_check_bluestore_slow_op_alert_de: BlueStore reported slow operations. Check the disk's health.
storage_reminders_tooltip: Configuration and security reminders from Ceph. They do not affect data or service, so they are not listed and do not change the state above. Fix them on the cluster, or silence them with ceph health mute.
storage_an_sub_pool: Sorted by the pool that fills first. Select a row to see it.
storage_an_sub_osd: Sorted by the fullest OSD. Ceph warns at {nearfull} and stops writes at {full}. Select a row to see it.
storage_an_sub_osd_plain: Sorted by the fullest OSD. Select a row to see it.
storage_an_sub_pvc: Sorted by the PVC that fills first, across all workspaces. Select a row to see it.
storage_an_never_reported: Not reported by kubelet in 7 days
storage_an_p95_tooltip: The 95th percentile of the 5-minute mean over the last hour. Ceph exports latency only as a sum and a count, so this is the closest to a p95 it allows.
workspace_storage_pvc_note_one: 1 PVC. Only mounted volumes report usage.
workspace_storage_pvc_note_many: {count} PVCs. Only mounted volumes report usage.
workspace_quota_gpu_shared_excluded: usage on {count} shared GPUs not counted
ws_analytics_sorted_cpu: Sorted by CPU requested, in cores.
ws_analytics_sorted_memory: Sorted by memory requested, in GiB.
ws_analytics_sorted_gpu: Sorted by GPU memory allocated, in GiB.
ws_analytics_quota_bars: Bars are shares of the workspace quota.
ws_analytics_select_row: Select a row to see it.
ws_analytics_pods_hint_workspace: Every pod in the workspace. Problems first.
ws_analytics_sub_volumes: One line per PVC, as a share of its capacity
ws_analytics_gpu_note_shared: {allocated} GiB allocated · usage on shared GPUs not counted
